proposal.direction: Increase interval 0 (steps 10–25) by +1 tick, holding intervals 1–3 at 5
proposal.hypothesis: Interval 0 has the least anti-aligned drift cosine (-0.020 mean) and the largest baseline effective guidance (max_atom_guidance_A ~0.00094 A) while clipping is zero. If the baseline under-delivers useful signal in this window, a one-tick increase there should move Mean upward relative to R0.
proposal.expected_mean_effect: Primary hypothesis: small positive Mean contribution versus R0; magnitude unknown because no one-tick response has ever been observed.
proposal.expected_best_effect: Best likely near-neutral; any Top10/Best change is a tradeoff, not a success gate.
proposal.falsifier: Mean(B-A) <= 0 with no compensating subgroup gain, or geometry at step 25/50 failing to shift at all, would refute 'interval 0 under-delivers' and close this direction.
proposal.diagnostic_alternative: If delivered displacement rises at step 25 but terminal core RMS_A is unchanged from R0, the limit is geometry response rather than delivery, and the next test should move to a different window instead of escalating amplitude here.
proposal.expected_subgroup_response: Baseline-quartile subgroups defined by R0: any gain should not be concentrated solely in the already-high q90 group; if it is, Mean gain will be small and the test is uninformative about the low tail.
proposal.revision_from_previous_result: No previous optimization result exists at bootstrap; this is the first non-baseline array and is anchored only to the R0 distributions.

proposal.direction: Decrease interval 0 (steps 10–25) by -1 tick, holding intervals 1–3 at 5
proposal.exploration_degree: low, single-component, opposite sign to H1
proposal.hypothesis: A reversal bracket is needed because sensitivity sign is unknown: if H1 gains, H2 should lose (monotonic response in this window); if H2 also gains, the baseline is over-driven in interval 0 and the useful direction is downward.
proposal.expected_mean_effect: Direction-identifying rather than payoff-seeking; symmetric in size to H1 so the pair can order the response without a noise claim.
proposal.expected_best_effect: Best expected roughly flat; a large Best drop with flat Mean would flag a concentration effect worth one follow-up.
proposal.falsifier: H1 and H2 both moving Mean the same way at similar size would show the effect is not a local amplitude response in interval 0, forcing a different window or component test.
proposal.diagnostic_alternative: Equal-sized moves in both directions imply batching or common-restoration context dominates over the edited interval; in that case no amplitude tuning of interval 0 is warranted.
proposal.expected_subgroup_response: If the response is symmetric-but-cancelling, expect opposite signs in the low and high R0 quartiles with near-zero net Mean; report that pattern instead of an average-only conclusion.
proposal.revision_from_previous_result: Bootstrap has no prior response; H2 exists solely to make H1's sign interpretable as a bracket rather than an escalation.

proposal.direction: Increase interval 3 (steps 76–90) by +1 tick, holding intervals 0–2 at 5
proposal.hypothesis: Interval 3 carries the largest baseline loss (mean 0.311) and the most anti-aligned drift cosine (-0.142 mean, q10 -0.385). A one-tick increase tests whether late-window delivery is under-supplied or actively counterproductive; both outcomes are decision-relevant because they would redirect effort away from late escalation.
proposal.expected_mean_effect: Pre-registered expectation is neutral-to-negative Mean versus R0 given anti-aligned drift, but the test is retained because the counter-case (late refinement helps) is cheap to exclude.
proposal.expected_best_effect: Most plausible Best route: late refinement could lift a few high-scoring candidates without moving Mean; this is explicitly a tradeoff, not a Mean gate.
proposal.falsifier: A clear Mean gain with unchanged Best would contradict the anti-gradient interpretation; a Mean loss with Best also falling closes late-interval escalation for the rest of the budget.
proposal.diagnostic_alternative: Endpoint and current-at-100 geometry aggregates are nearly equal in R0 (RMS_A 0.8051 vs 0.8062), so an unchanged endpoint after this edit would indicate late ticks barely propagate rather than that clipping removed them (clip_factor is 1.0).
proposal.expected_subgroup_response: Any late-window effect should be largest in candidates whose terminal core error is already small; a uniform shift across R0 quartiles would argue against a conformation-specific mechanism.
proposal.revision_from_previous_result: No prior trial; chosen over an interval-2 probe because interval 3 shows both the largest loss and the most negative drift cosine.

proposal.direction: Two-component exchange: raise interval 0 by +1 and lower interval 3 by -1, holding intervals 1–2 at 5
proposal.exploration_degree: medium, two changed intervals, opposite signs
proposal.hypothesis: If H1/H3 indicate amplitude is better spent early, shifting one tick from the most anti-aligned late window to the least anti-aligned early window should beat either single edit. If instead the edits are non-additive or context-dominated, this combination will not exceed the better single component, which is itself the informative outcome.
proposal.expected_mean_effect: Conditional on H1 and H3, expect Mean above R0 and at least matching the better single edit; additivity is not assumed.
proposal.expected_best_effect: Best expected within the range set by H1 and H3; no promise of a joint improvement.
proposal.falsifier: Combination Mean below both single-component results would show negative interaction, indicating separate edits cannot be composed in one round; equal-to-better-component would show the second edit is inert.
proposal.diagnostic_alternative: A shared offset from R0 across all four trials would void attribution to the edited intervals, since common restoration may begin before them and parent context can differ; the offset must be carried forward as unresolved.
proposal.expected_subgroup_response: If the exchange helps, gains should appear where interval-3 influence was largest at baseline; a flat response across quartiles would suggest the late interval was not contributing to these scores at all.
proposal.revision_from_previous_result: Bootstrap, so this combination is pre-registered as a conditional test whose interpretation depends on H1 and H3, not on any observed response.

proposal.direction: increase interval 0 (steps 10–25) by +1 tick; all other intervals fixed at 5
proposal.exploration_degree: low single-component perturbation at the earliest guided window
proposal.hypothesis: The 10–25 window has the largest baseline inside_rms_A (mean 4.3e-4 Å) and the mildest drift cosine (−0.035), so a small amplitude increase there should alter delivered displacement more than equivalent edits elsewhere and can shift Mean if affinity is sensitive to early-window motion.
proposal.expected_mean_effect: Unknown sign; if early displacement is under-delivered, small positive Mean contribution of order a fraction of a pIC50 unit, otherwise near zero.
proposal.expected_best_effect: Neutral to slightly positive; Best protection comes from retained incumbent TOP1, not this trial.
proposal.falsifier: paired_comparison(incumbent vs this trial) shows Mean(B−A)≤0 with no compensating subgroup gain, and geometry at step 25 shows negligible inside_rms change versus R0.
proposal.diagnostic_alternative: If displacement rises but Mean is flat, the discrimination is that affinity is insensitive to this window rather than that delivery was clipped (clip_factor is 1.0 at baseline).
proposal.expected_subgroup_response: If real, gains should be broad rather than confined to one A-quartile; uniform near-zero deltas would indicate insensitivity.
proposal.revision_from_previous_result: No prior optimization action; sensitivity unknown at bootstrap, so this is a first direction probe, not a correction.

proposal.direction: increase interval 3 (steps 76–90) by +1 tick; all other intervals fixed at 5
proposal.exploration_degree: low single-component perturbation at the most drift-negative window
proposal.hypothesis: The 76–90 window has the most negative baseline mean gradient_drift_cosine (−0.148) and moderate inside_rms_A (1.86e-4 Å); if late-window motion is the dominant lever on affinity, a one-tick increase should give the largest of the three single-window increase responses.
proposal.expected_mean_effect: Unknown sign; potentially the largest magnitude among H1/H2/H4 but no magnitude is claimed.
proposal.expected_best_effect: Unknown; a late-window change could shift the upper tail either way, so Best is reported, not gated.
proposal.falsifier: Mean(B−A)≤0 and no subgroup gain, or the paired delta is indistinguishable from the H1 probe, which would remove the late-window specificity claim.
proposal.diagnostic_alternative: Alternatively negative drift cosine marks unproductive motion; in that case H3's reversal, not H2, should improve Mean.
proposal.expected_subgroup_response: A concentrated response in the top A-quartile would suggest tail redesign; a diffuse response would suggest general stabilization.
proposal.revision_from_previous_result: No prior optimization action; the drift-cosine ordering motivates window choice but is not treated as evidence of benefit.

proposal.direction: decrease interval 3 (steps 76–90) by −1 tick; reversal bracket against H2
proposal.exploration_degree: low single-component reversal at the same window as H2
proposal.hypothesis: Paired with H2 this brackets the late window: if the H2 increase helps, the H3 decrease should hurt (monotone); if the H2 increase hurts, H3 decrease may help (local nonmonotonic response), so the pair resolves direction rather than escalating amplitude.
proposal.expected_mean_effect: Unknown sign; expected to be opposite in sign to H2 if the response is locally monotone, otherwise similar in sign.
proposal.expected_best_effect: Unknown; used as directional evidence, not as a Best claim.
proposal.falsifier: Both H2 and H3 move Mean in the same direction, or both are flat, which would refute a simple monotone late-window response.
proposal.diagnostic_alternative: A flat H2/H3 pair would point to window location insensitivity, making the mid-window H4 probe the residual discriminator.
proposal.expected_subgroup_response: Opposite-signed subgroup means between H2 and H3 in the same A-quartile would support a genuine directional effect; identical patterns would suggest insensitivity.
proposal.revision_from_previous_result: No prior optimization action; this reversal is pre-specified to convert the first late-window result into a direction decision.

proposal.direction: increase interval 1 (steps 26–50) by +1 tick; all other intervals fixed at 5
proposal.exploration_degree: low single-component perturbation at the intermediate window
proposal.hypothesis: The 26–50 window has intermediate drift cosine (−0.077) and lower inside_rms_A (2.1e-4 Å) than window 10–25; comparing it with H1 and H2 tests whether Mean response tracks delivered displacement magnitude, drift-cosine sign, or window position, keeping every other component matched.
proposal.expected_mean_effect: Unknown sign; intermediate magnitude expected if response scales with baseline displacement, near zero if drift sign dominates.
proposal.expected_best_effect: Unknown; reported alongside Top10 and median without being a success gate.
proposal.falsifier: Mean(B−A) flat while H1 or H2 shows a clear shift, which would indicate the mid window is not a lever; a shift as large as the late-window probe would weaken the drift-cosine ranking explanation.
proposal.diagnostic_alternative: If all three increase probes are flat, the residual alternative is that Mean is limited by factors outside these guided windows, including the untouched 91–99 band.
proposal.expected_subgroup_response: A window-specific pattern would appear as gains in different A-quartiles for H1 versus H4; a uniform pattern across windows would indicate a generic amplitude effect.
proposal.revision_from_previous_result: No prior optimization action; included to separate displacement magnitude from drift-cosine sign using matched single-component contrasts.
